title: GPU throughput vs quality: regional scenario workbook
content:
Executive summary:

This workbook explores concrete regional-capacity scenarios that trade off quantization level and batching aggressiveness against end-to-end output quality (measured on our internal multi-task eval set) and per-GPU throughput. The goal is to produce recommended GPU allocations per-region and a small experiment matrix to validate the best operating points by Q2 2026.

Key questions: 
- For a given latency SLO (p95 <= 220ms) and target quality budget (max -1.8% absolute accuracy across key tasks), how much GPU headroom do we free by moving from fp16 -> int8 -> int4?
- How far can we push batching (dynamic batching windows + max batch size) before quality or tail latency breaches occur?
- Which regions should use conservative profiles vs aggressive profiles for cost optimization?

Assumptions (baseline workload):
- Workload mix: 55% chat (avg seq in 1st turn: 120 tokens, followups 48 tokens), 35% completion-style (avg length 220 tokens), 10% embeddings/rerank (short).
- Traffic distribution: US-East 48%, EU-West 32%, APAC 20% (current 30-day aggregate).
- Token generation distribution: 65% short-turns (<60 tokens), 25% mid (60-300 tokens), 10% long (>300 tokens).
- Cache reuse: chat followups have 70% KV reuse on average, reducing per-token compute for followups.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms for single-turn interactive; batchable requests may have slightly higher latency allowance if the route is flagged as batch-friendly.
- Model variant: 7B baseline used for all scenarios; performance scaling factors applied per quantization profile.

Quantization profiles and measured deltas (internal eval):
- fp16 (baseline): throughput 1.0x, quality delta 0.0%
- int8 (q8): throughput 1.7x, quality delta -0.6% (task-weighted)
- int4 (q4): throughput 2.6x, quality delta -1.9%
- q4_k_m (mixed int4 heuristics): throughput 2.2x, quality delta -1.0%
Notes: numbers are latency- and kernel-optimized on A100-class GPUs with current runtime kernels. Throughput here is tokens/sec per GPU relative to fp16 baseline. Quality delta is model-eval task-weighted average on our regression suite (NLG coherence + summarization ROUGE + instruction-following classification accuracy).

Batching profiles and effective throughput multipliers (observed):
- Conservative batching (max_batch=8, batch_window=5ms): +1.15x throughput over single-request steady state, latency overhead consistent with SLO for 95% of traffic.
- Aggressive batching (max_batch=64, batch_window=25ms): +1.9x throughput but p95 latency often spikes >300ms on sporadic bursts without careful prioritization.
- Dynamic batching with latency-first prioritization: achieves ~1.5x on average and preserves p95 for latency-sensitive routes when combined with fractional preemption.

Scenario matrix (per-region estimates):
Columns: profile | per-GPU tokens/sec rel to fp16 | effective throughput multiplier (quant * batching) | estimated quality delta | suggested per-region conservative GPUs required for 1M tokens/day | suggested per-region aggressive GPUs required for 1M tokens/day

1) US-East (workload weight 48%)
- fp16 + conservative: 1.0x | 1.15x | 0.0% | 12 GPUs | 8 GPUs
- int8 + conservative: 1.7x | 1.955x | -0.6% | 7 GPUs | 5 GPUs
- q4_k_m + dynamic: 2.2x | 3.3x | -1.0% | 5 GPUs | 3 GPUs
- int4 + aggressive: 2.6x | 4.94x | -1.9% | 3 GPUs | 2 GPUs

2) EU-West (weight 32%)
- fp16 + conservative: 1.0x | 1.15x | 0.0% | 8 GPUs | 5 GPUs
- int8 + conservative: 1.7x | 1.955x | -0.6% | 5 GPUs | 4 GPUs
- q4_k_m + dynamic: 2.2x | 3.3x | -1.0% | 4 GPUs | 2 GPUs
- int4 + aggressive: 2.6x | 4.94x | -1.9% | 2 GPUs | 1 GPU

3) APAC (weight 20%)
- fp16 + conservative: 1.0x | 1.15x | 0.0% | 5 GPUs | 3 GPUs
- int8 + conservative: 1.7x | 1.955x | -0.6% | 3 GPUs | 2 GPUs
- q4_k_m + dynamic: 2.2x | 3.3x | -1.0% | 2 GPUs | 1 GPU
- int4 + aggressive: 2.6x | 4.94x | -1.9% | 1 GPU | 1 GPU

Interpretation notes:
- The per-region "GPUs for 1M tokens/day" numbers are rough ballpark for quick sizing. They assume average usable tokens/sec per GPU = base_tokens * (throughput multiplier) and 86,400 seconds/day; rounding applied.
- The quality deltas are on our internal weighted eval; different customers will observe different deltas depending on task mix. Use these deltas to allocate a "quality budget" per customer/route.
- The largest marginal gains come from moving fp16 -> int8 with conservative batching. Int4 yields more speed but crosses our default quality budget threshold (-1.8%). q4_k_m gives a pragmatic middle ground.

Risk and operational considerations:
- Tail latency: aggressive batching increases p95 spikes; must be coupled with a latency-first priority queue and request preemption to avoid user-visible regressions.
- Fallbacks: routes should have model-variant fallbacks (e.g., int4 fallback -> int8 -> fp16) and cross-region routing in case of capacity strain.
- Monitoring: add route-level quality metrics (mini-evals on production prompts) and more granular token/seq histograms per-region.
- A/B exposure: progressively roll quantized profiles behind canary flags and measure customer-facing metrics for 7–14 days before wide rollout.

Experiment plan (Q2):
- E1 (2 weeks): Deploy int8 + conservative batching in EU-West on 10% of traffic for low-risk routes. Track quality regression, latency SLOs, cost delta. Owner: Miguel (JIRA-ENGINF-821).
- E2 (3 weeks): Deploy q4_k_m + dynamic batching in APAC on non-latency-critical experiments and measure task-level delta and failure modes. Owner: Helen (JIRA-ENGINF-853).
- E3 (4 weeks): Controlled aggressive batching test in US-East behind preemption; use synthetic burst tests to tune batch_window and preemption thresholds. Owner: Jonas (JIRA-ENGINF-860).

Recommendations (initial):
- Short term (next 30 days): Allocate mixed profiles: US-East and EU-West default to int8 + conservative batching for 60% of routable capacity; reserve 25% fp16 for high-priority customers; keep 15% headroom for autoscale/burst. APAC defaults to q4_k_m for cost-sensitive workloads, with fp16 reserved for enterprise SLOs.
- Medium term (Q2): Run the experiment matrix above. If q4_k_m consistently shows < -1.0% delta and no customer regressions, expand to 30% of traffic for batch-friendly routes.
- Long term: Invest in kernel-level optimizations for int4 that's quality-preserving (model-wise quant-aware calibration) to push int4 operating points closer to -1.0% quality delta.

Operational checklist before rollout:
- [ ] Add small-production mini-eval harness that runs 2k route-specific prompts hourly and reports deltas per model-variant.
- [ ] Implement route-level fallback config UI in Console (canary rollouts + fallthrough model order).
- [ ] Add preemption + priority queue instrumentation to tracing and SLO dashboards.
- [ ] Update cost forecasting spreadsheet to include per-profile cost multipliers and estimated monthly saving projections.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quantization drift over time: do quality deltas change as prompts evolve? (need 6-week drift study).
- How do RLHF-tuned variants behave under q4_k_m vs int4 — currently unmeasured.
- Should we expose per-customer quality-budget controls in Console for enterprise customers to choose conservative/aggressive profiles?

Appendix: quick math example
- Baseline: fp16 GPU yields 1200 tokens/sec (measured) -> with conservative batching (1.15x) = 1380 tokens/sec effective.
- int8 throughput = 1.7 * 1200 = 2040 tokens/sec -> with conservative batching = 2040 * 1.15 = 2346 tokens/sec.
- For 1M tokens/day -> required GPU-days = 1,000,000 / (2346 * 86400) ~ 0.005, which scales to GPUs depending on 24/7 utilization; rounding and minimum allocation constraints apply.
